title: Shoulder Brake
intro: It's light and long, because endurance is what this is after, and nothing here stretches a shoulder that already lives at the end of its range. Racket Arm, also in the Care list, is a short roll and stretch. It doesn't load the shoulder, and this one does.

Do it after hitting or on a day you don't hit, and keep it out of the hours before you serve or play, because a tired shoulder makes overhead mechanics worse. The one exception is the Take the Edge Off block. Before you play, do two holds at an RPE of 6 instead of four. You need a band, something sturdy to anchor it to, like a knot in the band closed in a door, and something very light to hold. Check the band for nicks first. If it's no better after about six weeks, see a physio, or sooner if it's getting worse or coming on earlier than it used to.

before.label: Who it's for
before.text: A sore shoulder that a doctor or physio has already looked at and cleared you to train. If nothing hurts and you're just stiff overhead, this isn't your session. Open The Cage, in the Mobility list, is the one for that.

before.label: Stop and get it looked at
before.text: If your shoulder has come out or feels like it slips, there was a sudden pop while serving and you couldn't lift the arm, pain wakes you at night, the pain started after a fall, or you have pins and needles or numbness down the arm or coming from the neck. Chest pain, or shortness of breath along with the shoulder pain, means see a doctor the same day.

before.label: While you train
before.text: A bit of ache is fine. Sharp pain isn't, and neither is pain that builds through a set or feels worse the next morning. If it builds, stop that exercise. If it's sharp, stop the session. If an arm position pinches the front or top of the shoulder, stop that movement there.

good: Walk at an easy pace with your arms swinging
Feel your shoulders and back warming up
bad: Hunching your shoulders up as you walk

good: Make small slow circles with your arms straight out to the sides
Feel your shoulders loosen up with no pinch
bad: Making the circles bigger than feels comfortable

good: Hold the band at chest height and pull it apart to your sides
Feel your shoulder blades squeeze together
bad: Letting your arms drop below shoulder height

good: On hands and knees, put a hand behind your head and turn your elbow up to the ceiling
Feel the turn in your ribs and upper back
Lie on your side with your knees stacked and open your top arm out and back
Feel the turn in your ribs, not your lower back
bad: Chasing your top arm back past the point where the front of your shoulder pinches

good: Slide your forearms up a wall with your shoulder blades gliding round your ribs
Feel the muscle under your shoulder blade working
bad: Sliding up past the point where the front of your shoulder pinches

exercises.name: Band External Rotation
exercises.note: Sore side. On a flared-up day, do just this block at an RPE of 6 and don't mark the session done.

good: Anchor the band at elbow height with your elbow tucked in, then turn your forearm out and hold
Feel the back of your shoulder working to keep it steady
bad: Letting your elbow drift away from your side

exercises.name: Side Lying Dumbbell External Rotation
exercises.note: Sore side, 3s eccentric. If your shoulder feels worse the next morning than before you started, drop one set from each exercise in this block next time, and if it's still worse after that, get it looked at.

good: Lie on your side with the working arm on top, elbow at your ribs, and turn the dumbbell up toward the ceiling
Feel the back of your shoulder working
bad: Rolling your body back to lift the dumbbell higher

exercises.name: Prone Y Raise
exercises.note: 2s top hold. If a Y pinches, set your arms in a wide V instead.

good: Lie face down with your arms in a Y and your thumbs up, then lift them off the floor with nothing in your hands
Feel the muscles between your shoulder blades working
bad: Lifting your arms past the point where your shoulder starts to pinch

good: Pull the band to your ribs with your elbows tucked in
Feel your shoulder blades squeeze back and down
bad: Shrugging your shoulders up toward your ears
